grf.observed_reality: Production alias-DAG structural sharing and pair-memoized equality are merged, while _render_type_ref still expands every occurrence path when formatting diagnostics.
grf.generated_reality: The renderer is a separate resource surface: a tiny shared DAG can create a very large diagnostic even when canonicalization and equality are near-linear in distinct DAG nodes.
grf.counter_reality: Structural sharing alone might have bounded all TypeRef resource surfaces enough that renderer hardening would add complexity without measurable benefit.
grf.discriminator: Render a maximally shared binary TypeRef DAG using the exact current _render_type_ref algorithm while keeping the number of distinct immutable TypeRef objects tiny.
grf.outcome: COUNTER_REALITY_REFUTED; renderer expansion is independently unbounded by DAG sharing and requires a diagnostic-only bound.

unusual_experiment.shape: leaf I; each level P(child, child) reuses the same child object twice
unusual_experiment.result: At depth 18 only 19 distinct DAG nodes expanded into 1,572,859 diagnostic characters; this demonstrates occurrence-tree growth independent of structural object count.
unusual_experiment.rollback: No repository/runtime state changed by the experiment.

architecture_delta.proposal: Keep TypeRef identity/canonicalization/equality unchanged. Add a deterministic diagnostic-only render budget that preserves existing byte-identical output below the limit and emits an explicit bounded incompleteness marker when exact expanded output exceeds the admitted budget.
architecture_delta.reason_for_character_budget: A distinct-node cap alone is insufficient because shared occurrence paths can expand exponentially and identifier text itself can be large.
architecture_delta.counterhypothesis: Bounding diagnostics may hide a suffix that distinguishes two types; therefore bounded output must be explicitly marked incomplete and never feed type identity/equality or any authority decision.
promotion_tests: ordinary existing diagnostic strings remain byte-identical below the limit
deep non-recursive chains remain supported within the admitted budget
maximally shared DAG output/time/memory is bounded by the configured diagnostic budget rather than expanded-tree size
existing production TypeRef totality, alias totality, nominal typecheck and overlapping exact-head gates remain green
